title: Progressive tenant quarantine + multi-region swap playbook to protect Dedicated control-planes during rolling upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: minimize blast radius during Dedicated/Private control-plane rolling upgrades by introducing a progressive tenant quarantine and automated multi-region swap playbook. This ticket defines runbook steps, SLO-driven circuit thresholds, traffic routing primitives, and the rollout gating for upgrades so that a single misbehaving tenant or upgrade stage cannot push other tenants past latency/error SLOs. The outcome should enable safer rolling upgrades, faster rollback decisions, and clearer operator actions during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Automated quarantine action that removes ~<1% offending-tenant traffic fraction from upgraded nodes within 60s of breach detection
Region-swap orchestration that can divert affected tenant traffic to an alternate region with <300ms extra p95 latency for unaffected tenants
Upgrade gating metrics and dashboard (per-region, per-tenant) deployed to prod dashboards and used by CI canary checks
Playbook steps for operators documented and dry-ran in canary region with a simulated tenant spike
Integration tests added to upgrade pipeline to verify KV-cache warmup and traffic draining behavior
Rollback decision automated when aggregate p95 or error-rate crosses configured thresholds for >2 minutes
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation - add tenant-scoped SLI exports (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth) and a per-tenant token-bucket admission metric

Phase 2: Circuit & Quarantine primitives - implement a tenant quarantine controller that can: (a) apply token-bucket limits, (b) redirect a tenant to a warm spare pool, (c) mark tenant as quarantined in control-plane metadata
Phase 3: Multi-region swap - extend smart-routing to support active-passive tenant swap with traffic mirroring for verification and a fallback TTL
Phase 4: Upgrade gating - add canary promotion policy that requires stable tenant SLIs for 10m and KV-cache hit-rate > 80% before wider rollout
Phase 5: Runbook & automation - publish operator playbook, set automated rollback triggers, and add a post-incident report template
Phase 6: Chaos & verification - run fault-injection tests (node drain, degraded network, sudden tenant burst) in staging and a single canary region
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Quarantine is too aggressive and harms customer latency. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, staged rollout, and a quick-unquarantine API
Risk: Region swap causes cold-start latency for KV-heavy tenants. Mitigation: pre-warm KV caches via shadowing and staged request replay before swap
Risk: Automated rollback oscillation during flapping networks. Mitigation: require sustained threshold breaches (e.g., 2m) and backoff timer before re-trying upgrades
Risk: Operational complexity. Mitigation: single-button runbook steps in Console and clear operator dashboards showing per-tenant state
notes: Design trade-off: quarantine + token-bucket preserves fairness vs global load-shedding which would be simpler but penalizes healthy tenants
We prefer region-swap over immediate fallback to lower-tier models because it preserves correctness for low-latency use-cases
Consider exposing a developer opt-in quarantine policy for customers to accept temporary reduced throughput during upgrades
This ticket coordinates closely with networking (for cross-region routing), infra (for warm spare pools), and console for operator UX
